review_detail: Christopher Nolan delivers a visual and intellectual treat. The concept of dreams within dreams is executed flawlessly. The score by Hans Zimmer elevates the tension to incredible heights. One of the best sci-fi movies of the decade.
I found the movie far too convoluted for its own good. It tries to be smart but just ends up being a maze of exposition. The action scenes were decent, but the emotional core was lacking.
Everything about this movie is perfect. The acting, the directing, the pacing. DiCaprio gives one of his best performances. I've watched it five times and still find new details.

The Dark Knight transcends the superhero genre. It's a gripping crime thriller. Heath Ledger's Joker is arguably the greatest cinematic villain of all time. The pacing is relentless and the themes are surprisingly deep.
It's a fantastic movie, no doubt. But the third act feels a bit rushed and Two-Face's arc could have used more breathing room. Still, a monumental achievement in comic book movies.
Pandora is gorgeous and the 3D effects are groundbreaking. However, the story is just Dances with Wolves in space. It's predictable and the characters are somewhat one-dimensional.
James Cameron pushed the boundaries of CGI and performance capture. The world-building is spectacular. I didn't mind the simple story because the experience itself was so immersive.
Michael Bay's signature explosions cannot hide the terrible script, wooden acting, and incomprehensible action sequences. A massive waste of money and time. Pure garbage.

If you turn off your brain and just enjoy the spectacle, it's a great time. The visual effects of the robots transforming are incredible. Optimus Prime is badass. Exactly what I wanted for a summer movie.
Jordan Peele's directorial debut is a masterclass in building tension. The social commentary is sharp and the horror elements are genuinely unsettling. Daniel Kaluuya is fantastic.
